description: Twelve logic and comparison results worked out from two input voltages, all computed at once and all available together.

inputs.text: The voltage called A in every result; any voltage other than 0V counts as true, and the number of channels patched here sets the module's polyphony.
The voltage called B in every result; any voltage other than 0V counts as true.

outputs.text: 10V while both A and B are away from 0V, otherwise 0V.
10V while either A or B is away from 0V, otherwise 0V.
10V while exactly one of A and B is away from 0V, otherwise 0V.
10V while both A and B are at 0V, otherwise 0V.
10V while A is below B, otherwise 0V.
10V while A is above B, otherwise 0V.
10V while A is below B or equal to it, otherwise 0V.
10V while A is above B or equal to it, otherwise 0V.
10V while A and B are at exactly the same voltage, otherwise 0V.
10V while A and B differ by any amount, otherwise 0V.
1V while A is at 0V, otherwise 0V; one volt rather than the ten every other output on the panel gives.
1V while B is at 0V, otherwise 0V; one volt rather than the ten every other output on the panel gives.

notes: Both A and B must be patched. With either one empty no output is written at all, so each jack holds whatever it last carried, which is 0V on a freshly placed module.
